tools.name: list_formats
tools.description: List the Pokémon Champions regulations this connector supports, with each one's id, dates, whether it is current, team rules, number of legal Mega Evolutions and whether usage statistics are available. Use it to find the `format` value other tools accept and to see which format they use by default.

tools.description: Get a Pokémon's types, base stats, abilities, weight, alternate forms and any Mega Evolutions legal in the supported regulations (with the Mega's types, ability and base stats). tools.name: analyze_team_types
tools.description: For a list of Pokémon, count how many are weak to, resist or are immune to each attacking type, and report shared weaknesses, types nothing on the team resists, and defensive types that would patch the most gaps. It considers typing only — not abilities, items or moves — and suggests types, not spec

tools.name: get_top_usage
tools.description: Rank the most-used Pokémon in a regulation by the share of ladder teams they appear on, from the most recent month of usage statistics loaded for that regulation (the month itself is not reported; get_usage_trend shows dated history). Use it to see what a team should expect to face. Mega Evolutions

tools.name: get_pokemon_usage
tools.description: Show how one Pokémon is typically built in a regulation: its usage and rank, and the most common abilities, items, moves and stat spreads as a share of its recorded sets. Spreads use the stat-point scale the ladder records (0–32 per stat in Pokémon Champions).

tools.name: get_teammates
tools.description: List the Pokémon that most often share a team with the given Pokémon in a regulation, as the share of its teams that include each one. Use it to find proven partners and cores.

tools.name: get_checks_and_counters
tools.description: List the Pokémon that most reliably beat the given Pokémon on the ladder, ranked by Smogon's checks-and-counters score. The data records one-on-one outcomes (a knockout or a forced switch), so in doubles treat it as a rough signal. Pokémon with few recorded matchups have no data.

tools.name: get_usage_trend
tools.description: Show one Pokémon's monthly usage and rank in a regulation across a range of months, with its net change and peak. History exists only for months the regulation's ladder was active.

tools.name: get_meta_shifts
tools.description: Compare a regulation's usage between two months: the biggest risers and fallers, Pokémon that newly reached meaningful usage and Pokémon that dropped out. Use it to see how the metagame changed. Needs at least two months of history.

tools.name: get_usage_momentum
tools.description: Fit a trend to each Pokémon's monthly usage across a range and list the fastest rising, fastest declining and most volatile. These are descriptive trends, not forecasts. Needs at least three months of history in the range; with so few points, treat the result as a direction, not a measurement.

tools.name: calculate_damage
tools.description: Calculate how much damage one move does from one Pokémon to another in Pokémon Champions doubles: the damage range, the share of the defender's HP, and the chance to knock it out. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: analyze_team_types · Private data: get_pokemon_usage, get_checks_and_counters · Public sink: analyze_team_types, get_top_usage, get_pokemon_usage, get_teammates, calculate_damage · Destructive: list_formats, lookup_pokemon.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: analyze_team_types · Private data: get_pokemon_usage, get_checks_and_counters · Public sink: analyze_team_types, get_top_usage, get_pokemon_usage, get_teammates, calculate_damage · Destructive: list_formats, lookup_pokemon

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
